sections.h2: Fast sale options in North Miami
sections.html:
A homeowner here can accept cash, list with an agent or go it alone, and the deadline plus the state of the house point to the right one. Whichever you choose, the deed, title search and Miami-Dade recording are identical. Repair cost, waiting time and your final take are what move.

  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies, a negotiable closing date, house taken as is.
  • Agent listing: a larger pool of buyers, with showings, an inspection period and a lender's schedule.
  • Owner sale: no listing fee, but the contract and buyer screening are yours.

Ask for two written offers and compare what you would keep after costs. Offers that look close can end far apart once repairs, stamp tax and carrying months are counted.

North Miami is a suburban city in northeast Miami-Dade County, about ten miles north of downtown Miami. The city counts more than 64,000 residents, which makes it the sixth largest in the county, and it incorporated on February 5, 1926. Biscayne Bay lies along the east side, and the Biscayne Bay Campus of Florida International University is nearby. Oleta River State Park and the Museum of Contemporary Art at MOCA Plaza are local landmarks.

Homes near the water and the university draw different buyers than homes inland, and renters and investors are a steady part of the market.

sections.h2: Local rules to check before you sell
sections.html:
Code compliance is the first office to call. It sends violation notices to the owner of record and not the tenant, which makes any open violation at your address your job to clear before closing.

Rentals are tightly limited. Advertising a rental for less than three months is prohibited, and so is renting for three months or less or renting more than four times in a twelve month period. If your house has hosted short stays, buyers will raise it, so stop them before you list.

  • Ask code compliance whether the address has open violations or an unfinished inspection.
  • Keep the right-of-way in front of the lot maintained, since owners are responsible for it.
  • Do not divide a single-family home into units without permits from the city's Building Department.
  • Ask whether a certificate of use or business tax receipt is attached to the property.

The code compliance phone line is on the city website. A call before you list costs less than hearing about a problem from the buyer's title company. If a violation is open, ask what it takes to close it and how long that usually runs, then weigh fixing it against selling as is at a lower price.

sections.h2: Taxes and fees at a North Miami closing
sections.html:
The biggest state charge on a deed is the documentary stamp tax. Miami-Dade runs its own schedule of 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and a document conveying only a single-family dwelling skips the surtax. The rate in the rest of Florida is 70 cents.

Closing items on a North Miami deed
Closing itemAmount or rule
Deed stamp tax, Miami-Dade60 cents per $100, plus 45 cents per $100 surtax (not due on a single-family dwelling only)
Liability for the taxAll parties to the document are liable
Clerk recording, first page$5.00
Clerk recording, each added page$4.00
Collected byCounty clerk, at recording

The statute adds small extra charges per page, so the title company's settlement statement shows the final recording total. Mortgage payoffs, association fees and prorated property tax come out of your proceeds at closing.

Assessed value is locked in on January 1, and November brings the tax collector's bills. The Miami-Dade appraiser's homestead page sets March 1 as the application deadline and accepts late filings until the cutoff on the proposed tax notice, usually 25 days after mailing. Renewal receipts do not go to properties with a change of ownership, deeds by warranty or quitclaim included.

The exemption belongs to the owner and does not stay with the house. A new buyer applies on their own, and the sale moves the assessed figure up to market level on the next January 1.

Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year. For owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, it raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028. From 2029 the amount is adjusted for positive consumer price index changes, and the school board portion stays at $25,000.

Newcomers are treated differently. Someone who becomes a Florida resident after the start of 2027 may start with up to $50,000 against non-school taxes, and generally reaches the higher amount in the fifth year of holding a homestead. That five-year rule is subject to federal constitutional limits and to implementing legislation.

Do not quote a buyer's future tax bill in a listing. Send buyers to the county appraiser's homestead page and phone number and let them confirm what applies to them.

Yes to both, with strings attached. For an inherited house, the title company wants to see who may sign: probate letters, or proof the property passed outside probate. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's list of documents that owe no stamp tax.

With a tenant, hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. Some cash buyers accept the tenant and others want the unit empty at closing. North Miami limits short rentals, so confirm any short-stay use was lawful before you describe it.

Moving the house to a relative first can add cost, since quitclaim deeds are on the taxable list and may change how the county treats ownership.

sections.h2: What is a sensible timeline for a sale?
sections.html:
Clean title lets a cash sale close in as little as a couple of weeks. Add a lender and the appraisal and loan approval stretch the schedule. Allow time for payoff letters, an association estoppel and clearing any permit or violation.

  • First week: gather the deed, tax bill, payoff and association papers.
  • Next: pick an offer and a closing date.
  • Then: title search, lien and violation clearing, signing appointment.
  • Closing: signing before witnesses or a notary, then recording.

A contract with a firm date and a plain list of seller repairs prevents the most common slips. If anyone on the deed lives far away, ask the closing agent about remote signing arrangements early so the date does not slide.

faqs.q: What is the stamp tax rate on a deed in North Miami?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax, and the surtax is not due when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Your title company can give the figure for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I rent the house short term while it is listed?
faqs.a: No. Rentals of three months or less are prohibited, as is renting more than four times in twelve months. Check with code compliance before any short stay.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the sale resets assessed value to market level the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for a code violation notice at my address?
faqs.a: The city addresses the notice to the owner. A tenant should speak with the landlord, but plan to clear the violation before closing.

faqs.q: What is Amendment 3 and when does it start?
faqs.a: Voters approved it on November 3, 2026. It takes effect January 1, 2027 and first applies to the 2027 tax year, raising the non-school homestead exemption for eligible owners.
